scenario.name: Microsoft Threat Intel & Elastic DFIR — ISO / VHD Virtual Disk Mount, Zone.Identifier ADS & LNK Shellbags Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a customs inspection checkpoint that stamps a bright red overseas warning label onto every shipping crate downloaded from the internet. A smuggler packs a poisoned shortcut inside a sealed virtual steel shipping container so only the outer crate gets the red warning stamp; when an employee double-clicks the crate to mount it as a fresh drive letter, the shortcut inside walks out completely unlabelled, yet forensic investigators catch the full delivery chain through the outer crate stamp, the virtual-drive mounting log, and the user folder-viewing diary. In this scenario (T1566.002, Microsoft Threat Intel & Elastic DFIR, ISO / VHD Virtual Disk Mount, Zone.Identifier ADS & LNK Shellbags Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: container Download, then virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys, then uSRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\\ Navigation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Container Download, then Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys, then USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\\ Navigation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 15 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation (Sysmon EventID 15)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1566.002 - Spearphishing Link & Mark-of-the-Web ADS)
stages.description: When an employee downloads a phishing-delivered virtual disk archive through a browser, the filesystem attaches a hidden customs tag straight onto the outer archive file recording both that it came from the public internet and the exact web address that hosted it. When the user downloads Invoice_Oct.vhd from an external webmail link, the browser writes the NTFS Alternate Data Stream Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier containing [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 (Internet), ReferrerUrl, and HostUrl. Sysmon EventID 15 (FileCreateStreamHash) captures the exact Contents of the Zone.Identifier stream (logged in Sysmon Event 15 with EventID=15 , Sysmon FileCreateStreamHash, AlternateDataStream=Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier, ZoneId=3 , URLZONE_INTERNET, HostUrl=https://portal.doc-delivery.net/Invoice_Oct.vhd so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 15 (FileCreateStreamHash): TargetFilename=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 15 , FileCreateStreamHash: TargetFilename=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1566.002 during "Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation , Sysmon EventID 15" , When the user downloads Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ADS Content: [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 ReferrerUrl=https://mail.external-share.com/ HostUrl=https://cdn.external-share.com/Invoice_Oct.vhd runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ADS Content: [ZoneTransfer] ZoneId=3 ReferrerUrl=https://mail.external-share.com/ HostUrl=ht so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1566.002 during "Container Download & NTFS Zone.Identifier Alternate Data Stream Creation , Sysmon EventID 15" , When the user downloads Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ msedge.exe writing C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd:Zone.Identifier / ⇠#1 ACK 15) from Node ① (#1 Malicious Container (Invoice.vhd)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Mounted Volume E:\ (.lnk + DLL)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys & Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1 / 12
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1553.005 - Subvert Trust Controls: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass)
stages.description: Double-clicking the downloaded container prompts the operating system virtual-disk engine to mount it cleanly as a new removable drive letter such as E: silently writing mount and surface timestamps into the system virtual-disk logbook. When the user double-clicks Invoice_Oct.vhd, Windows Explorer mounts the virtual hard disk via the VHD Miniport Driver (vhdmp.sys) as drive E:\. Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational logs EventID 1 (VHD surfaced as disk number 2) and EventID 12 (File C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd opened as virtual disk). Prior to Windows 11 22H2 / KB5019959, FAT32/UDF files inside ISO/VHD containers did not inherit the outer MotW Zone.Identifier (logged in WinEvent Event 1 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational, EventID=1 , VHD Surfaced / 12 , VHD Handle Opened, MountedContainerPath=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd, MountedDriveLetter=E:\ , DiskNumber 2 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.title: Stage 3: USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution (LECmd & SBECmd)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1204.002 - User Execution: Malicious File & LNK/Shellbag Artifacts)
stages.description: Inside the newly opened virtual drive window, the user clicks a disguised document shortcut that launches the hidden payload without SmartScreen warnings, while Windows Explorer quietly records the drive visit inside the user Shellbags diary and records the shortcut metadata. Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct.lnk (which hides a hidden E:\rundll32_loader.dll). Under the hood, the observed step executes SBECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses USRCLASS.DAT BagMRU for E:\ (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , SBECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses US so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1204.002 during "USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution , LECmd & SBECmd" , Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact LECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses Invoice_Oct.lnk target args runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , LECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent" --csv C:\Forensics # P so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1204.002 during "USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution , LECmd & SBECmd" , Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). steps.plainTitle: Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys & Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1 / 12
steps.storyAnalogy: Double-clicking the downloaded container prompts the operating system virtual-disk engine to mount it cleanly as a new removable drive letter such as E: silently writing mount and surface timestamps into the system virtual-disk logbook.
steps.simpleExplanation: When the user double-clicks Invoice_Oct.vhd, Windows Explorer mounts the virtual hard disk via the VHD Miniport Driver (vhdmp.sys) as drive E:\. Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational logs EventID 1 (VHD surfaced as disk number 2) and EventID 12 (File C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd opened as virtual disk). Prior to Windows 11 22H2 / KB5019959, FAT32/UDF files inside ISO/VHD containers did not inherit the outer MotW Zone.Identifier (logged in WinEvent Event 1 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational, EventID=1 , VHD Surfaced / 12 , VHD Handle Opened, MountedContainerPath=C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd, MountedDriveLetter=E:\ , DiskNumber 2 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1: VHD C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd surfaced as Disk #2 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1: VHD C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\Invoice_Oct.vhd s so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1553.005 during "Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys & Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1 / 12" , When the user double-clicks Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 12: Virtual disk handle opened by System (PID 4) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 12: Virtual disk handle opened by System , PID 4 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1553.005 during "Virtual Disk Mount via vhdmp.sys & Microsoft-Windows-VHDMP-Operational EventID 1 / 12" , When the user double-clicks Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).

steps.plainTitle: USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution (LECmd & SBECmd)
steps.storyAnalogy: Inside the newly opened virtual drive window, the user clicks a disguised document shortcut that launches the hidden payload without SmartScreen warnings, while Windows Explorer quietly records the drive visit inside the user Shellbags diary and records the shortcut metadata.
steps.simpleExplanation: Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct.lnk (which hides a hidden E:\rundll32_loader.dll). Even after the attacker unmounts E:\ and deletes Invoice_Oct.vhd, Windows Explorer records the user browsing E:\ inside USRCLASS.DAT (Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU) and creates a Jump List / Recent LNK record in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\ containing the LNK TrackerDataBlock MachineID and VolumeDroid (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate, LnkTargetCommand=rundll32.exe E:\rundll32_loader.dll,DllRegisterServer, ShellbagArtifact=USRCLASS.DAT\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU , Drive E:\, RecentLnkArtifact=%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\Invoice_Oct.lnk so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes SBECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses USRCLASS.DAT BagMRU for E:\ (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , SBECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses US so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1204.002 during "USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution , LECmd & SBECmd" , Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact LECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent" --csv C:\Forensics # Parses Invoice_Oct.lnk target args runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , LECmd.exe -d "C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent" --csv C:\Forensics # P so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1204.002 during "USRCLASS.DAT Shellbags E:\ Navigation & Weaponized .LNK Execution , LECmd & SBECmd" , Inside the newly mounted E:\ drive, the user opens E:\Invoice_Oct while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
